outcome: Executive function (Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function for Adults)
cohort: Female patients aged >=18 years, either with a history of preeclampsia or a normotensive pregnancy, studied between 6 months and 30 years after their first pregnancy, excluding those with pre-existing hypertension, autoimmune, or kidney disease.
finding: Women with a history of preeclampsia were 9 times more likely to experience clinical attenuation of higher-order cognitive functions compared to women with normotensive pregnancies, with elevated risks persisting for decades.
mod_finding: Method of delivery was not related to overall executive function.
